D1.name: Hiring Readiness Optimization
D1.comparative_analysis: Plan 1 covers the NLP technical stack well (NLTK, SpaCy, BERT, Hugging Face, fine-tuning) and includes a dedicated Month 5 for interview prep and portfolio polish, but interview preparation is concentrated at the end rather than distributed throughout. Plan 2 integrates interview prep goals into every single month, includes ML system design whiteboarding, behavioral STAR method practice, and DSA applied to NLP contexts from Month 1. Plan 2's capstone ('Smart Customer Support Assistant') is a single coherent end-to-end project that gets deployed to cloud with Docker and FastAPI, making it significantly more employer-worthy. Plan 1's portfolio is more fragmented across monthly mini-projects without a unified deployable artifact. Plan 2's technical coverage also includes RAG and LLMs which are highly relevant for 2024-2025 NLP hiring.
D1.winner_reason: Plan 2 distributes interview preparation across all 5 months, builds a single deployable capstone with cloud deployment, and covers modern NLP tooling (RAG, LLMs, MLOps) that directly maps to current NLP Engineer hiring criteria.

D2.name: Time-Constrained Feasibility
D2.comparative_analysis: Plan 1 allocates 30 hours/month for 5 months = 150 hours total, which matches the available hours exactly with no buffer. Plan 2 calculates 120 total hours (1hr/day × ~4 weeks × 5 months, accounting for ~24 days/month), plans 108 hours, and reserves 12 hours as buffer — this is more realistic and disciplined. However, Plan 2's cognitive load is heavier: Month 1 asks the user to master advanced Pandas, SQL, linear algebra, and begin a capstone pipeline simultaneously. Plan 1's Month 1 is more focused on NLP fundamentals. Plan 2 also introduces RAG, Docker, and cloud deployment in Month 4 which is ambitious for 22 hours. Both plans are aggressive for 1 hour/day, but Plan 2's explicit buffer and hour tracking is more honest about constraints.
D2.winner_reason: Plan 2 explicitly tracks total available hours, plans within them, and reserves a 12-hour buffer, demonstrating more disciplined time management than Plan 1's exact-fit 150-hour allocation with no buffer.
